caption: Fragments of the Great Eleusinian Relief, showing Demeter, Triptolemos, and Persephone (Roman copy of a Greek original, c. 450-425 BC).
alt: Ancient marble relief of three standing figures: a mature woman on the left, a nude young man in the center reaching up, and a robed woman on the right holding what may have been torches or sheaves.
credit: Marie-Lan Nguyen (User:Jastrow) / Wikimedia Commons. Original fragments in the National Archaeological Museum, Athens; cast at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (14.130.9).
note: The hosted text is the Project Gutenberg edition of Evelyn-White's translation and has no illustrations. This is not a page of that edition; it is the closest thing to a primary image of the myth itself: an ancient relief showing the scene at the heart of the Hymn, Demeter and Persephone sending Triptolemos out with the gift of grain. Chosen over a modern illustration per the brief's guidance for the two Eleusinian-mysteries texts. Downscaled from the original 2390x3450 to keep the file under 2MB; attribution required under CC BY 2.5.
